diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, if $G$ has a unique fixed-point, then $(\widehat{\mu}_t)_{t\in\N_0}$ converges $\PROB$-almost surely in $\CW_2$ to the Wasserstein barycenter of $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ with weights $w_1,\ldots,w_K$.

We would like to remark that the operator~$G$ in (\ref{eqn: G-operator}) does not always have a unique fixed-point for general input probability measures $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K\in\CP_{2,\mathrm{ac}}(\R^d)$; see, e.g., Example~3.1 of \citep{alvarez2016fixed} for a concrete counterexample.

issues.failure_explanation: The general conclusion established by the main theorem is almost-sure precompactness with fixed-point accumulation points. Convergence of the entire sequence to the barycenter requires the additional uniqueness-of-fixed-point hypothesis. The paper expressly acknowledges that this hypothesis is not generally available. Thus the abstract and repeated broad descriptions omit a central condition and advertise a stronger guarantee than the formal results establish.

failure_location.quote: This gives rise to a computationally tractable stochastic fixed-point algorithm which is provably convergent to the 2-Wasserstein barycenter.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify all barycenter-convergence claims by uniqueness of the fixed point of G. Without that hypothesis, advertise only precompactness and fixed-point accumulation, not convergence to the barycenter.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised guarantee for general continuous non-parametric barycenter problems is unsupported, even if the conditional convergence proofs are repaired.
issues.title: Unconditional barycenter convergence is advertised, but only conditional convergence is proved
issues.why_classification: The supported correction changes the central guarantee from general barycenter convergence to a conditional or subsequential fixed-point guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\CX_\mu$ and $\CX_\nu$ be two connected bounded open sets in $\R^d$ that both have $\CC^2$-boundaries and are both uniformly convex.

issues.failure_explanation: The boundary hypotheses do not support the asserted higher-order regularity up to the boundary. For q=2, take uniform measures on a ball and on a uniformly convex C2 domain that is not C3. Their constant densities meet the hypotheses. The claimed C4,α potential, together with the positive Monge–Ampère determinant, would give a nondegenerate C3,α transport diffeomorphism mapping the sphere onto the target boundary. That would make the target boundary C3, contradicting its choice.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Impose boundary regularity appropriate to the requested derivative order, for example smooth uniformly convex boundaries, and propagate that restriction to the support and truncation classes used by the entropic specialization.
issues.overall_effect: The higher-order global regularity used to justify the concrete entropic estimator is not established for the declared C2 admissible support class.
issues.title: Arbitrary-order global transport regularity is claimed from only C2 boundaries
issues.why_classification: This requires a substantive regularity restriction, but smooth supports, balls, ellipsoids, and a comparable non-parametric method remain available without changing the global convergence architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion is false at α=1, independently of boundary smoothness. In dimension two, let P3(x)=Re((x1+i x2)^3) and u(x)=|x|²/2+εχ(|x|)P3(x)log|x|, with a smooth cutoff supported inside the unit ball. For small ε, u is strongly convex, ∇u is the identity near the boundary, and det D²u is positive and Lipschitz, whereas D²u is not Lipschitz. Here Δ(P3 log r)=6P3/r² is Lipschitz, and the determinant's quadratic remainder is also Lipschitz. Change of variables makes ∇u the OT map from density det D²u/|B| on B to the uniform law on B. issues.title: The global regularity theorem includes an invalid Lipschitz endpoint

We will refer to $\CM^q(\R^d)$ as the set of $q$-admissible compactly supported probability measures.

issues.failure_explanation: Regularity of the transport Hessian does not remove jumps of the densities at their support boundaries. Let μ=ν be uniform on a ball. This pair belongs to every stated admissible class and has the identity OT map with constant Hessian. Its Wasserstein geodesic is constant, but the density extended by zero to R^d has a boundary jump; its square root is not in H1, so its Fisher information, and hence I0, is infinite. The term involving I0 therefore cannot be absorbed into a finite C_entr as the proof does.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish an entropic bias/consistency estimate that handles these support-boundary jumps, or redesign the admissible class and reprove the estimator analysis. Merely adding finite Fisher information is incompatible with the current positive compact-support construction.
issues.overall_effect: The concrete entropic consistency proof and its convergence corollary are unsupported for the very compact, positive-on-support densities used by the paper.
issues.title: Finite integrated Fisher information is falsely inferred for compact positive densities
issues.why_classification: The available bound becomes vacuous on basic admissible examples, and preserving the advertised concrete estimator guarantee requires a new analysis rather than a local hypothesis insertion.
